title: Status asthmaticus — auto-PEEP after intubation
learnerTitle: ED resus 2 — 24F, severe asthma, just intubated
summary: 24F with severe asthma intubated in the ED 10 minutes ago; now hypotensive with high airway pressures from dynamic hyperinflation.
objectives: Recognize dynamic hyperinflation: expiratory flow not returning to zero, rising auto-PEEP, hypotension
Disconnect from the ventilator as a diagnostic and therapeutic step
Set low RR, short Ti and long expiratory time; accept hypercapnia
Measure auto-PEEP (expiratory hold) and plateau pressure
Maximize bronchodilators, systemic steroids, IV magnesium

chart.hpi: Lifelong asthma, 2 prior ICU admissions, one prior intubation (age 19). 3 days of URI symptoms, then 12 h of worsening wheeze despite home albuterol every 1–2 h. Arrived tripoding, speaking single words, SpO2 88%. Continuous albuterol, ipratropium, methylprednisolone 125 mg and magnesium 2 g given; became drowsy with a silent chest and was intubated with ketamine/rocuronium (8.0 ETT). Placed on VC 450, RR 28, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.4.
chart.social: Graduate student. Vapes nicotine. Has a cat.
chart.exam: Sedated. Very diminished breath sounds bilaterally with faint expiratory wheeze. Prolonged expiration. Trachea midline. Neck veins distended. Cool hands.

stages.name: Breath stacking + hypotension
stages.nurse: Her pressure is dropping and the vent keeps alarming high pressure.
stages.cue: RR 28 with long time constant → auto-PEEP ~11. Look at the flow trace: expiration never reaches zero. Expect: disconnect, RR 10–12, Ti 0.8, check auto-PEEP, keep bronchodilators.

branches.label: Disconnects from vent / lowers RR and lengthens expiration
Increases RR to fix the CO2

stages.name: Auto-PEEP relieved
stages.nurse: Her BP came right up after we disconnected. CO2 is 62 now — is that OK?
stages.cue: Permissive hypercapnia; pH ≥7.20 acceptable. Re-check auto-PEEP and plateau (<30). Continue bronchodilators via in-line neb, steroids, consider ketamine infusion.

stages.name: Worsening stacking — near arrest
stages.nurse: BP is 64 systolic and peaks are over 50!
stages.cue: Dynamic hyperinflation → obstructive shock. Disconnect now, gentle lateral chest compression to exhale, then low RR. Rule out tension pneumothorax (POCUS).

branches.label: Disconnects + manual chest compression to exhale
Needle decompression without evidence of pneumothorax

a.text: Expiratory hold: total PEEP 16 cmH2O with set PEEP 5 → auto-PEEP 11 cmH2O.

b.text: Expiratory hold: total PEEP 6 cmH2O with set PEEP 5 → auto-PEEP ~1 cmH2O.

c.text: Expiratory hold: total PEEP 19 cmH2O with set PEEP 5 → auto-PEEP 14 cmH2O.

a.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 25 cmH2O; Ppeak 48 cmH2O (large peak–plateau gap = high airway resistance).

b.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 14 cmH2O; Ppeak 36 cmH2O.

c.text: Inspiratory hold: Pplat 28 cmH2O; Ppeak 52 cmH2O.

a.text: Prolonged hiss of exhaled air for ~20 s after disconnection; BP rises to 104/60 within a minute.

c.text: Long exhalation after disconnection; BP recovers to 98/58.

cxr.text: Portable AP: ETT 5 cm above the carina. Marked hyperinflation with flattened hemidiaphragms. No pneumothorax. No focal consolidation. No pneumomediastinum.

lus.text: Lung sliding present bilaterally (anterior and lateral). A-line pattern. No B-lines. No effusion.

echo_pocus.text: Small, hyperdynamic, underfilled LV and RV. No pericardial effusion. IVC distended (2.3 cm) without respiratory variation.

rvp.text: Rhinovirus/enterovirus DETECTED. Influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2 not detected.

ecg.text: Sinus tachycardia 128. Right axis deviation. No ST changes.

ct_chest.text: Hyperinflation, bronchial wall thickening, mucus plugging in both lower lobes. No pneumothorax. (Transport: SBP fell to 70 during the move.)

albuterol.text: In-line continuous albuterol started via the ventilator circuit.

methylpred.text: Methylprednisolone 125 mg was given in the ED 40 min ago; 60 mg IV q6–8h ordered.

mag.text: Magnesium 2 g IV was given in the ED; second 2 g dose infusing.

teaching: Post-intubation hypotension in asthma is dynamic hyperinflation until proven otherwise — disconnect first.
Expiratory time is the lever: RR 10–12, Ti 0.7–0.8 s, high inspiratory flow; minute ventilation matters more than VT.
Peak–plateau gap reflects airway resistance; plateau and auto-PEEP reflect hyperinflation risk.
Permissive hypercapnia is expected; pH ≥7.20 is usually tolerated.
Ketamine (bronchodilating) is a reasonable sedative; avoid histamine-releasing agents.
